quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on roadways. You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign. Do not proceed until the intersection is clear and you can safely pass through.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few mph faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few mph slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to the traffic around you when it is within the speed limit. Vehicles traveling at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: As your speed increases, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop as you go faster. When driving at high speeds, look far ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When someone is tailgating you, add extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to prevent a collision.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:

options.text: You first come to a complete stop.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in the lane for a green arrow, you may proceed in that direction when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: If a driver sees pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should the driver do?

options.text: Keep going. The driver has the right-of-way.
Let the pedestrians cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the pedestrians cross the street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the pedestrians have crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, use your turn signal:

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
When pulling to the curb, but not when leaving it.
When pulling to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when pulling to a curb or leaving a curb.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines in work zones are the same as on regular roads.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to stop for equipment. Driving carefully protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to return to the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you cannot see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, move back to the right lane when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may proceed at a safe speed if the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may proceed at a safe speed if the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you may proceed through the intersection. Yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection and go when it is safe.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, check:

options.text: Only the left side mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder toward the direction you are changing lanes to check your blind spot.

questions.question: If your car's suspension is bad, it can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and provides a comfortable ride. If your vehicle bounces too much after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A work zone is ahead.
No one may pass.
Either direction may pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either direction may pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates traffic in opposite directions. Either driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
Will always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you proceed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that the right lane is ending. Be prepared for merging traffic.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Follow the car ahead more closely.
Pass carefully and do not stare at the work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully and do not stare at the work.
questions.explanation: Do not "rubberneck" or slow down to look at unusual things. This causes traffic congestion and is unsafe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hospital.
Intersection ahead.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to an upcoming intersection. Prepare for possible traffic or turns.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left, right, then left again before entering an intersection. Check for approaching vehicles and pedestrians. Look to your left a second time since vehicles from that direction will be closer. Make sure the entire path through the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and need more distance to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When it is very foggy, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them with your low beams.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no one can pass in either direction.

questions.question: When you merge onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
5 to 10 mph slower than the freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of traffic on the freeway.

questions.question: When a child on a bicycle is near your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Assume the child has full control of the bicycle.
Be ready for anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable and may change direction suddenly. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: The light turns yellow as you approach an intersection at the speed limit. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Yellow means caution and the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even if you signal.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Go through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, finish crossing safely. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that traffic must move in one direction only. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
There is roadwork or maintenance ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork or maintenance ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs mark construction, maintenance, and utility work areas. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Fines for violations may double in these areas.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus uses flashing lights and a stop arm when loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a steady speed to regain traction.
Press the brakes hard to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When water on the road causes hydroplaning, your tires lose contact with the pavement. Slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: Motorcycles and scooters are hard to see, so you should:

options.text: Drive slowly.
Look around constantly.
Share your lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in blind spots. Always look carefully for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds.

questions.question: To pass safely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Use your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed of oncoming vehicles. Make sure you have enough space to change lanes safely. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle passes.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield the right-of-way to any driver who:

options.text: Is on your left.
Arrived before you.
Is across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. If vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down, you should:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on the highway, turn on your emergency flashers and move off the road away from traffic if possible. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its signal arm extended, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are present.
Drive normally but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely and stay stopped when a school bus has flashing lights and its arm extended. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction. Wait until the arm retracts and the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends.
Be ready for workers and equipment.
Change lanes and keep your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment.
questions.explanation: Signs in work zones warn of workers, equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Where can you safely pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles.
Where signs and road markings allow passing.
On a curve with no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleys. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and markings permit it.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
Your protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
